verdict.rationale: Square's Terminal API is documented as the way to connect a custom POS application with a Square Terminal, and it includes checkout options such as a separate tip screen. Payment webhooks let a backend observe results. The evidence does not explicitly show the server-to-terminal flow (creating checkout requests from a backend and the terminal picking them up), so coverage of the server-driven part is only partial. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of backend-initiated terminal checkout requests and their lifecycle (create, cancel, status), Terminal API endpoint references, and independent or hands-on corroboration of a custom POS integration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a custom point-of-sale checkout that drives the terminal from my backend through a documented server-driven API

citations.quote: Use the Terminal API to connect a custom POS application with a Square Terminal.
Tip money: Collect tips as money at checkout. Supports showing a separate tip input screen before getting a buyer's signature and allowing custom tip amounts.
supports webhook events that notify you when a payment is created or updated.
